To fabricate, assemble, repair and service mechanical equipment/systems towards ensuring equipment reliability and plant availability, in a safe and cost-effective manner and compliance with applicable policies, procedures and regulatory statutes.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
Equipment Assembling / Installations & Commissioning
· A  Analyse and interpret blueprints of mechanical equipment/systems (diagrams, drawings, specifications & plans to determine suitable material and sequence of operations).
·     Measure and mark out materials for fabrication
·     Fabricate and/or construct structural components, monitor process and adjust settings
·     Inspect fabricated components make corrective changes where necessary
·     Assemble and fit fabricated components into tools, equipment or systems
·     Keep record of all installation activities
·     Participate in equipment/system commissioning to ensure that the equipment/system is in good and safe functional condition.

Mechanical Maintenance (Predictive / Preventative / Corrective and Shutdown)

·    Ensure adequate inventory/availability of necessary spares and/or supplies.
·    Create suitable maintenance schedules in liaison with production management.
·    Perform preventative and corrective maintenance activities as per Plant Safety Regulations, preventative maintenance plans and maintenance procedure
·    Conduct maintenance as per Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) maintenance procedure.
·    Ensure personal and team members' safety.
·   Perform plant Shutdown work as per shutdown plan.
·   Conduct fault-finding and problem-solving on mechanical, hydraulic, pumps and pneumatic equipments.
·    Conduct overhauling of all mechanical equipments.
·    Attend to breakdowns, conduct PM's, perform standby duties and after hours' callouts as and when necessary.
·    Ensure that all machinery complies with General Machinery Regulations (GMR) and that all work is done in accordance with relevant SANS codes.
·    Uphold and maintain quality standards and ensure that customer requirements are addressed.
·    Ensure that equipment/machines produce products that are within quality specifications and address non-conformances that are caused by mechanical mal functioning.

Condition Monitoring
·     Inspect and monitor the conditions of equipment regularly and record accordingly as per Planned Maintenance schedule and submit report to management.
·    Interpret deviations recorded and take corrective actions to rectify when applicable.
·    Inspect conveyors, pipes and tanks
·    Take and maintain vibration monitoring records for all critical plant rotating equipment
Compliance to all Safety, Health, Environment, Risk, Quality & Food Safety (SHERQFS) Standards and Regulations
·    Maintain cleanliness of equipment and work area.
·    Ensure that housekeeping activities conform to Food Safety Regulations.
·    Conduct safety checks on all machinery and tools and ensure completion of safety checklists as required.
·    Comply with Company SHERQFS procedures and instructions. '
·    Report all health and safety and food safety risks and problems.
·    Collaborate with SHERQFS personnel when implementing remedial actions.
·    Attend to emergency situations in accordance to procedures such.
Maintenance Procedures & Training
·     Provide input into maintenance Standard Operating Procedures.
·     Train colleagues/apprentices to install, maintain or repair mechanical equipment and systems, and on SOPs as and when applicable.
Continuous Improvement
·     Identify opportunities for improvement of plant performance.
·     Initiate and implement improvement programs and initiatives as approved by management.

Among other tasks, your main responsibilities will include:
Debtors administration and invoicing

• Escalating long-outstanding, disputed or high-risk accounts to management in line with internal procedures.
• Monitoring adherence to payment plans and following up immediately when agreed payments are missed.

• Verifying payments received and allocating receipts accurately to the correct debtor accounts and invoices.
• Reconciling debtor ledgers, bank receipts, CRM records and accounting system balances.
• Investigating and resolving unallocated receipts, short payments, overpayments and other account discrepancies.
• Assisting with month-end debtor reconciliations and ensuring outstanding items are supported and followed up.
• Maintaining accurate and complete audit trails for all debtor transactions and adjustments. Queries and reporting
• Acting as a key point of contact for debtor and invoice-related queries from clients, advisors and internal teams.
• Resolving billing and payment queries promptly, professionally and with appropriate supporting documentation.
• Preparing debtor ageing reports, collection updates and other reports on outstanding balances and payment trends.
• Working closely with finance and operational teams to improve debtor processes, reporting and controls. Administrative support
• Managing a shared inbox and reassigning emails to the correct staff member.
• Converting relevant university marketing emails into notices so that important information can be shared with staff members.
• Maintaining data and contacts on the CRM by gathering the correct email addresses from university representatives. Additional finance support
• Monitoring commission payments due from partner universities and following up on outstanding amounts.

• Supporting system and process improvements, including CRM and Xero integration or automation initiatives. About Sable International

This is not for a call centre. This customer centric, multi-skilled role   supports the sales & purchasing departments.

The company located in Alrode, Alberton is a subsidiary of a large global group. They provide local industrial technology, specializing in compression technology components, gas-powered engine sales and parts, and field maintenance services for the energy and process industries.
A strong work ethic, performance driven with stable work history are valued attributes.
This closely-knit successful SA team value their people and have an extremely low turnover.
Remuneration - Approximately R25-R28k gross basic + Excellent benefits i.e., Co. contributes 50% of medical aid up to Discovery Cassic Priority regardless of dependents; Co. contributes up to 10.5% of basic n terms of retirement fund; guaranteed 13th + discretionary additional bonus based on individual & Co.'s performance up to 12% of  annual salary.
Overview - Role requires an individual who communicates effectively with customers, suppliers & colleagues, addresses their concerns and ensures a seamless exerience with their products and services. Strong problem-solving skills & a customer-centric approach is necessary. You would be performing clerical / administrative support duties for the sales & purchasing departments. Prepare & distribute various sales reports when required. Maintain customer & supplier files, assist sales team & handle inquiries about products or services. Project a professional company image through all interactions.
Key Responsibilities:
Customer Interation -  Respond to customer inquiries via phone, email and online channels regarding required services and parts. Check & assist with reviewing internal costings leading to preparing customer quotations.
Supplier Interaction - Obtain RFQ's from suppliers based on customer requirements. Respond to vendor inquiries via phone, email and online channels. Prepare Vendor Purchase Orders, monitor supplier deliveries.
Order Management -  Process customer orders, ensuring accuracy in product specifications, delivery dates, Incoterms and payment details. (Capture orders and goods received notes on relevant systems, eg: SAP/Service Next. Procure spares, co-ordinate deliveries, Raise, send & save documentation.
Import & Export Control - Prepare & collate required documentation and deal with freight forwarders to obtain Import Licenses, enure that correct Inco-terms are being applied.
Issue Resolution - Handle customer complaints or issues, escalating to the appropriate department when necessary, while maintaining a professional and positive demeanor.
Sales Support - Assist with upselling parts, service agreements, and additional products based on customer needs.
Documentation - Maintain accurate records of customer interactions, transactions, inquiries, and complaints in relevant systems.
Collaboration - Work closely with the sales, technical support, and stores teams to ensure timely and accurate delivery of products and services as well as controlling/maintaining stock levels in relation to open sales orders and customer contracts. Liase with the workshop  regarding processing of Job cards/picking lists and production orders.
Follow-up - Proactively follow up on customer satisfaction, order status and any post-purchase support needs.

With more than 34400 students, and approximately 1700 members of staff, the Durban University of Technology (DUT) is a leading university of technology proudly located in the beautiful cities of Durban and Pietermaritzburg, along the warm east coast of South Africa. Founded in April 2002 through the historic merger of the former ML Sultan Technikon and Technikon Natal, DUT has evolved into a modern, metropolitan, multi-campus university with roots tracing back to 1907.
Today, DUT is recognised nationally and internationally for its excellence in teaching and learning, research, innovation, entrepreneurship and engagement. A proud member of the International Association of Universities, DUT continues to expand its influence across South Africa and the world. In the 2025 Webometrics Rankings, DUT was ranked among the Top 6% of all universities and colleges worldwide, reflecting its academic excellence, research impact and strong global visibility.
DUT’s Philosophy of Education, “Our creativity and innovation shapes adaptive graduates who transform society” reflects the institution’s deep commitment to meaningful impact for societal transformation. Guided by its inspirational and aspirational ENVISION2030 strategy, which is rooted in DUT’s DNA of being ‘people-centred and engaged’ and ‘innovative and entrepreneurial’ and underpinned by its bespoke Living Values Framework, DUT focuses on ‘contributing to the improvement of lives and livelihoods’.
The University comprises six diverse Faculties:
• Accounting and Informatics
• Applied Science
• Arts & Design
• Engineering and the Built Environment
• Health Sciences
• Management Sciences
DUT also includes a Business School and the award-winning Institute for Water and Wastewater Technology (IWWT), amongst other research centres and institutes, reinforcing its role as a hub for knowledge, innovation and societal impact. Over the years, the University substantially grown its research output, dominating the UoT sector. This is evidenced by the steady increase of NRF-rated researchers and the notable, unprecedented award of seven NRF SARCHi Chairs in 2025. This impetus helps us to remain deeply engaged with our communities glocally, thereby transforming societies and economies.
At DUT, we believe in nurturing talent and empowering people to make a real difference. If you are passionate about contributing to education, research, innovation, entrepreneurship and engagement, DUT offers the ideal environment - Creative. Distinctive. Impactful.

Our client is seeking a detail-oriented and customer-focused Short Term Claims Junior Assessor to support the accurate, fair, and timely assessment of homeowners' insurance claims. This role focuses exclusively on buildings and structural (non-motor) claims, ensuring that claims are assessed in accordance with policy terms, regulatory requirements, and internal claims standards.
Working closely with the Short Term Claims Team, the successful candidate will assist in evaluating claims, validating policy cover, gathering supporting information, and progressing claims efficiently while delivering exceptional customer service. This is an excellent opportunity for an individual looking to develop a career in short-term insurance claims assessment.
Key Responsibilities
Claims Assessment & Processing
• Assess allocated homeowners' insurance claims in accordance with policy terms, conditions, exclusions, and limits.
• Gather and verify all supporting documentation from policyholders, contractors, service providers, and internal stakeholders.
• Assess claims for indemnity, ensuring accurate application of excesses, policy conditions, and settlement calculations.
• Escalate complex, disputed, or high-value claims to senior assessors with clear supporting documentation.
• Process approved claims within delegated authority while maintaining compliance with internal controls.
Buildings & Structural Claims Support
• Conduct desktop assessments using photographs, contractor reports, repair quotations, and supporting documentation.
• Assist with site inspections under the guidance of senior assessors where required.
• Evaluate repair quotations and scope-of-work documents, identifying discrepancies or areas requiring further investigation.
• Assess common homeowners' claims including:
• Storm damage
• Fire damage
• Burst pipes
• Geyser failures
• Power surge claims
• Subsidence and structural damage
• Apply building and structural knowledge when evaluating claims and determining appropriate outcomes.
Fraud Identification & Risk Management
• Identify potential fraud indicators during the assessment process.
• Escalate suspicious claims promptly in accordance with company procedures.
• Verify supporting documentation and investigate inconsistencies where necessary.
• Promote fraud awareness through accurate claim validation and reporting.
Regulatory Compliance
• Ensure all claims comply with applicable Short-Term Policyholder Protection Rules (PPRs).
• Apply Treating Customers Fairly (TCF) principles throughout the claims process.
• Maintain complete, accurate, and auditable claim records.
• Ensure assessment decisions comply with company policies and regulatory requirements.
Customer & Stakeholder Engagement
• Provide professional and empathetic service to policyholders throughout the claims process.
• Keep customers informed of claim progress and manage expectations effectively.
• Liaise with brokers, contractors, suppliers, and internal Claims Consultants to facilitate claim resolution.
• Escalate complaints or customer concerns in line with internal procedures.
Continuous Learning & Development
• Participate in coaching, mentorship, and formal training programmes.
• Keep up to date with policy wording changes, regulatory developments, and claims best practices.
• Participate in quality reviews, calibration sessions, and team meetings.
• Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives within the claims department.

job_title: Researcher/Senior Researcher in Accumulation and Inequalities in the RASC (Contract post)
about_role:
Readvertisement: Researcher/Senior Researcher in Accumulation and Inequalities in the Rhodes African Studies Centre (RASC)
(Contract post – 2 years)
The Rhodes African Studies Centre invites suitably qualified candidates to join their team.
The Rhodes Africa Studies Centre (RASC)
Established in 2019, the Rhodes African Studies Centre is an inter-faculty research Centre of Excellence that is located in the Faculty of Humanities at Rhodes University. It focuses on conceptual, methodological, and empirical ways of reconfiguring African studies. The Centre is an integral part of Africa Multiple, an initiative of the DFG’s Excellence strategy. Africa Multiple comprises the University of Bayreuth in Germany; Moi University in Kenya; University of Lagos in Nigeria and the University of Joseph Ki Zerbo in Burkina Faso, in addition to University of Salvador du Bahia, which is one of our partners. For more information, visit Africa Multiple at: https://www.africamultiple.uni-bayreuth.de/en/index.html
Main Objectives
Research is the main focus, and teaching is not a core function.  Where the researchers are on contract, raising funds for their employment, contract research shall be regarded as equivalent to more traditional forms of research.
In assessing the candidate’s scholarship for promotion, consideration will be given to the individual's track record.  While disciplinary differences are considered, the candidate must demonstrate standing within the discipline through their research and student research.  This could mean that the individual has demonstrated leadership, made a major contribution to research projects, served as the lead author on publications, or consistently contributed to multiple publications throughout their academic career.
The Requirements
Researcher
• A PhD in African Studies, Political Economy, Economics, Political Sciences, Sociology, Science and Technology Studies, Gender Studies, Anthropology, Geography, Urban Planning, History, Cultural Studies, or a related field.
• Some experience in areas related to accumulation and inequality research, as well as political economy thinking; a focus on the gendered nature of accumulation dynamics is desirable.
• Emerging publication profile in leading journals with a reference to the themes "accumulation" and "inequality". A strong monograph by a respected publisher can be credited as an alternative. The publications address inter- and/or transdisciplinary research projects and build on proven collaborations relevant to the theme of accumulation and inequalities.
• Postgraduate research supervision is not necessarily required. Those with such experience have an added advantage.
• Some experience in coordinating or organising interdisciplinary and/or collaborative projects and/or programmes (this may include conferences and related academic activities)
• Evidence of attendance and presentation at local conferences. Presentation at international conferences will be an added advantage.
• A scholar showing significant research potential.
• Administrative experience, including the ability to coordinate a team of scholars in a collaborative international and interdisciplinary research context.
Senior Researcher
• A PhD in African Studies, Political Economy, Economics, Political Sciences, Sociology, Science and Technology Studies, Gender Studies, Anthropology, Geography, Urban Planning, History, Cultural Studies, or a related field.
• Significant expertise and experience in areas related to accumulation and inequality research, as well as political economy thinking; a focus on the gendered nature of accumulation dynamics is desirable.
• A very good publication record in leading journals with a reference to the themes "accumulation" and "inequality". A strong monograph by a respected publisher can be credited as an alternative. The publications should address inter- and transdisciplinary research projects and build on proven collaborations relevant to the theme of accumulation and inequalities.
• Research supervision of at least a Master’s degree is required. Supervision at the PhD level will be an added advantage.
• Significant experience in leading and/or coordinating interdisciplinary and/or collaborative research projects and/or programmes.
• Evidence of attendance and presentation in local and preferably international conferences.
• An established researcher with an emerging national profile in the discipline.
• Track record of administration, management, and/or leadership roles (leadership roles may be informal) in a collaborative international and interdisciplinary research context.
Application Process
It is essential that prospective candidates read the job profile for further information and ensure that all relevant documentation is submitted.
The following documents are required:
• A comprehensive CV and relevant qualifications which should include the following: -
• Reasons for leaving your current and previous jobs.

Please refer to the academic role profile and further particulars document for further information.

Senior Researcher

Role Purpose:
The Lending Dealmaker will be required to originate, structure, negotiate and execute profitable lending (Working Capital, Commercial Property finance and Term Loan) and structured finance transactions for mid-market corporate clients by developing trusted client relationships, identifying funding opportunities and coordinating internal stakeholders through to successful financial close.
The Transactor is accountable for the entire client lifecycle, from business development and opportunity identification through credit approval, execution, drawdown and ongoing portfolio management; while balancing client needs, commercial returns and prudent risk management
Main Accountabilities:
• Origination
• Originate and develop quality lending opportunities that align with Merchant West's strategic objectives, risk appetite and return requirements.
• Develop and maintain a sustainable pipeline of bankable transactions through proactive business development, referrals and relationship management.
• Identify, engage and convert new clients while deepening relationships with existing clients and strategic partners.
• Understand clients' funding requirements and develop bespoke financing solutions that create long-term value.
• Market, present and articulate credit opportunities to internal stakeholders, Credit Committees, institutional funders and other capital providers.
• Coordinate and manage the end-to-end transaction process from initial engagement through credit approval, documentation and funding.
• Prepare high-quality term sheets, transaction proposals, credit papers, investment memoranda, client presentations and other supporting documentation.
• Transaction Structuring
• Structure innovative and commercially viable financing solutions that balance client requirements with Merchant West's risk and return objectives.
• Develop funding structures suitable for institutional investors and other funding partners.
• Assess alternative financing structures and recommend the most appropriate solution based on commercial, legal, tax and funding considerations.
• Work collaboratively with Credit, Legal, Treasury and external advisers to optimise transaction structures and facilitate successful execution.
• Contribute to product development, process improvements and strategic initiatives as required.
• Transaction Execution and Portfolio Management
• Manage the successful implementation of approved transactions through close coordination with Credit, Legal, Operations, Treasury and external stakeholders.
• Ensure legal documentation accurately reflects approved commercial terms and all conditions precedent are satisfied prior to funding.
• Oversee transaction drawdown and successful financial close.
• Monitor the ongoing performance of the portfolio through financial reviews, covenant monitoring and proactive client engagement.
• Identify emerging credit risks and implement appropriate remedial actions where required.
• Maintain awareness of economic, industry and regulatory developments that may impact client performance and portfolio quality.
• Credit Evaluation & Assessment
• Conduct comprehensive commercial, financial and credit assessments of prospective transactions.
• Analyse historical and forecast financial information, cash flows, repayment capacity, management capability, industry dynamics and security structures.
• Identify key transaction risks and develop appropriate mitigants and structural protections.
• Prepare clear, balanced and well-supported credit recommendations for approval.
• Apply sound commercial judgement when evaluating pricing, risk-adjusted returns, return on equity (ROE), capital utilisation, portfolio concentration, correlation risk and overall transaction profitability.
• Relationship Management
• Develop and maintain trusted relationships with clients, introducers, institutional investors, professional advisers and internal stakeholders.
• Build a strong internal network across Origination, Credit, Legal, Treasury, Finance and Operations to facilitate efficient transaction execution.
• Act as a trusted adviser by developing a thorough understanding of clients' businesses, industries and strategic objectives.
• Deliver exceptional client service while maintaining an appropriate balance between commercial opportunity and prudent risk management.
• Represent Merchant West professionally, demonstrating the highest standards of integrity, accountability and collaboration..

• Demonstrated experience in corporate banking, commercial banking, structured finance, leveraged finance, asset finance, private credit or business banking, with a proven ability to originate, structure and execute debt transactions.

This is a rare opportunity to do work that genuinely matters. A women's health research team based at a public hospital in Westdene, Johannesburg, operates through a clinical research unit focused on cervical cancer prevention and sexual and reproductive health. The team runs rigorous, protocol-driven clinical trials, with a strong track record of meaningful research in women's health, including work with women living with HIV. The environment is academic, purpose-led, and deeply committed to advancing health outcomes for women in South Africa.
This is not a routine nursing role. The successful candidate will play a central part in bringing a new clinical trial to life, from recruiting and enrolling participants through to managing study visits, collecting and processing specimens, and maintaining the kind of meticulous documentation that good clinical research demands. If you thrive in a structured yet fast-moving environment, enjoy working across clinic, pharmacy, and lab teams, and want your clinical skills to contribute directly to research that reaches real communities, this role was built for you.
What's in it for you
Be part of meaningful, purpose-driven research focused on cervical cancer prevention and women's health.
Join a well-regarded, experienced research team with a history of high-quality clinical trials.
Build and apply a rare combination of clinical and research skills in a single role.
Work in an academic environment that values precision, initiative, and continuous learning.
Contribute findings that are shared with community stakeholders and have real-world impact.
Minimum Requirements
Registered professional nurse, enrolled nurse, or equivalent qualification recognised by the South African Nursing Council.
Active registration with the South African Nursing Council at the time of application.
Valid Good Clinical Practice (GCP) certification and training in the protection of human subjects.
Minimum two years of experience in clinical research or public health.
Spoken and written fluency in English and IsiZulu or Sesotho.
Strong computer literacy with solid writing and presentation skills.
Demonstrated experience in clinical research.
Demonstrated experience in cancer, sexual and reproductive health, or HIV programmes.
Excellent attention to detail and accuracy in documentation and data capture.
Ability to manage multiple priorities, work independently, and take initiative.
Clinical experience in women's sexual and reproductive health services such as Pap smear screening, STI screening, or family planning is a strong advantage.
Prior experience in clinical trials is advantageous.
Valid Basic Life Support (BLS) certification is advantageous.
Willingness to work overtime or weekends when required.
Key Responsibilities
Assist the study coordinator and investigators with planning, setting up, and managing day-to-day clinical trial activities in line with the approved protocol, GCP, and SOPs.
Recruit participants and support screening, enrolment, and ongoing retention through follow-up, reminder calls, and tracing of participants lost to follow-up.
Administer and accurately document informed consent for all study participants.
Schedule and coordinate study visits, liaising with clinic, pharmacy, and laboratory staff to ensure smooth visit flow.
Provide health education to participants, including HIV pre- and post-test counselling and results counselling.
Perform study procedures including vital signs, phlebotomy, pregnancy tests, pelvic examinations, Pap smears, HPV tests, and STI tests.
Administer investigational products or study drugs as directed.
Support collection, processing, labelling, storage, and tracking of all biological specimens.
Maintain accurate, complete, and contemporaneous source documents, case report forms, study logs, and participant records.
Capture study data into the electronic data capture system, resolve data queries, and support quality control of records.
Assist with assessing, documenting, and reporting adverse events and protocol deviations to the study coordinator and investigators.
Help maintain the investigator site file and support readiness for monitoring visits, audits, and regulatory reporting.

Provide routine clinical care as requested.

job_title: Postdoctoral Research Fellowship: Wildlife Science, Wildlife Management and Conservation Biology (1-
about_role:
The Department of Animal Science at the University of the Free State (UFS), South Africa, invites applications for a Postdoctoral Research Fellowship in Wildlife Science, Wildlife Management and Conservation Biology.
Candidates interested in pursuing an academic or professional career in Wildlife Science, Wildlife Management, Conservation Biology, Rangeland Ecology, Wildlife Monitoring and Sustainable Natural Resource Management are encouraged to apply.
The successful candidate will join an active multidisciplinary research programme focused on understanding the ecological, biological, nutritional and conservation factors regulating African wildlife populations, with particular emphasis on large herbivores, habitat utilisation, wildlife monitoring, sustainable rangeland management and evidence-based conservation planning.
The fellowship provides an opportunity for a talented doctoral graduate to gain advanced research, teaching and postgraduate supervision experience under the mentorship of established researchers while contributing to internationally recognised research programmes.
The fellowship will be awarded on a competitive basis, considering applicants' academic achievements, publication record, teaching experience, supervisory experience and research potential. The fellowship is available for a period of one year and is renewable annually for up to three years, subject to satisfactory performance and the submission of annual progress reports.
Duties and responsibilities:
•    Conduct innovative research in wildlife science, wildlife management and conservation biology.
•    Contribute to research on wildlife monitoring, habitat assessment, sustainable rangeland management, conservation planning and large herbivore ecology.
•    Utilise modern technologies including GPS telemetry, GIS, remote sensing, drones and artificial intelligence within wildlife research programmes.
•    Publish a minimum of two peer-reviewed scientific papers per year.
•    Present research findings at national and international scientific conferences.
•    Assist with undergraduate teaching and practical training in Wildlife Science and Wildlife Management.
•    Assist with the supervision and mentoring of Honours, MSc and PhD students.
•    Contribute to curriculum enhancement and module development.
•    Assist with grant applications and research project development.
•    Register and reside as a postdoctoral fellow at the University of the Free State and participate in relevant activities of the Directorate of Research and Postgraduate Studies.
Job Requirements:
Eligibility criteria
•    Open to all South African and foreign nationals for full-time research at the University of the Free State.
•    Hold a PhD degree in Wildlife Science, Wildlife Management, Conservation Biology, Ecology, Zoology, Rangeland Science, Animal Science or a closely related discipline.
•    Have obtained their doctoral degree within the last five years.
•    Demonstrate a publication record in peer-reviewed scientific journals.
•    Have experience in wildlife research and field-based ecological studies
•    Demonstrate experience in undergraduate teaching and practical training.
•    Demonstrate the ability to contribute to curriculum development and postgraduate supervision.
•    Possess excellent scientific writing and communication skills.
•    Hold a valid driver's licence (attach a copy).
•    Successful applicants may not hold full-time salaried employment during the fellowship period.
•    Successful applicants must be willing to relocate to Bloemfontein and participate fully in departmental research, teaching and postgraduate activities.
Application:
To apply, please email the following documentation by 21 August 2026 to Prof Francois Deacon at deaconf@ufs.ac.za. Late applications will not be considered.
•    Motivation letter detailing research experience, teaching experience, publication record and suitability for the fellowship.
•    Full Curriculum Vitae, including a list of publications, conference presentations and other scholarly outputs.
•    Full academic transcripts and copy of doctoral degree certificate.
•    Copy of ID document or passport.
•    Contact details of three academic referees.
Value of the fellowship:
•    R 270,000 annual fellowship.
•    R 30,000 additional research expenses fund.
Closing date:
21 August 2026
Commencement of fellowship:
01 January 2027

This is not for a call centre. This customer centric, multi-skilled role   supports the sales & purchasing departments.
It is preferred that you come from a manufacturing / technical environment with similar experience as described below.  English is the main language used however, fluency in French would be advantageous but not essential.
The company located in Alrode, Alberton is a subsidiary of a large global group. They provide local industrial technology, specializing in compression technology components, gas-powered engine sales and parts, and field maintenance services for the energy and process industries.
A strong work ethic, performance driven with stable work history are valued attributes.
This closely-knit successful SA team value their people and have an extremely low turnover.
Remuneration awaiting confirmation - Approximately R25k neg. gross basic + Excellent benefits i.e., Co. contributes 50% of medical aid up to Discovery Cassic Priority regardless of dependents; Co. contributes up to 10.5% of basic n terms of retirement fund; guaranteed 13th + discretionary additional bonus based on individual & Co.'s performance up to 12% of  annual salary.
Overview - Role requires an individual who communicates effectively with customers, suppliers & colleagues, addresses their concerns and ensures a seamless exerience with their products and services. Strong problem-solving skills & a customer-centric approach is necessary. You would be performing clerical / administrative support duties for the sales & purchasing departments. Prepare & distribute various sales reports when required. Maintain customer & supplier files, assist sales team & handle inquiries about products or services. Project a professional company image through all interactions.
Key Responsibilities:
Customer Interation -  Respond to customer inquiries via phone, email and online channels regarding required services and parts. Check & assist with reviewing internal costings leading to preparing customer quotations.
Supplier Interaction - Obtain RFQ's from suppliers based on customer requirements. Respond to vendor inquiries via phone, email and online channels. Prepare Vendor Purchase Orders, monitor supplier deliveries.
Order Management -  Process customer orders, ensuring accuracy in product specifications, delivery dates, Incoterms and payment details. (Capture orders and goods received notes on relevant systems, eg: SAP/Service Next. Procure spares, co-ordinate deliveries, Raise, send & save documentation.
Import & Export Control - Prepare & collate required documentation and deal with freight forwarders to obtain Import Licenses, enure that correct Inco-terms are being applied.
Issue Resolution - Handle customer complaints or issues, escalating to the appropriate department when necessary, while maintaining a professional and positive demeanor.
Sales Support - Assist with upselling parts, service agreements, and additional products based on customer needs.
Documentation - Maintain accurate records of customer interactions, transactions, inquiries, and complaints in relevant systems.
Collaboration - Work closely with the sales, technical support, and stores teams to ensure timely and accurate delivery of products and services as well as controlling/maintaining stock levels in relation to open sales orders and customer contracts. Liase with the workshop  regarding processing of Job cards/picking lists and production orders.
Follow-up - Proactively follow up on customer satisfaction, order status and any post-purchase support needs.

about_role:
The University of the Free State invites applications from visionary, innovative and strategic leaders for the position of Senior Director: Directorate for Institutional Research, Strategic Analytics and Institutional Effectiveness and Planning (DIRSIP). Reporting to the Deputy Vice-Chancellor: Strategic Initiatives, International and Institutional Affairs, the Senior Director provides strategic leadership for institutional planning, strategy implementation, institutional research, business intelligence, statutory reporting, project portfolio management and enrolment planning.
The incumbent will play a pivotal role in supporting evidence-based decision-making, organisational effectiveness and the successful implementation of the University's Vision 130 and strategic priorities.  As a member of the University's senior leadership community, the successful candidate will lead the University's institutional planning and performance management functions while ensuring that strategic information supports sound governance and executive decision-making.
Duties and responsibilities​​​​
Strategic Plan Tracking
•    Coordinate the implementation of Vision 130, the Strategic Plan, and the Annual Performance Plan.
•    Steer strategy, institutional research and operational projects.
•    Monitor the Key Performance Indicators across all portfolios, faculties and divisions.
Executive Decision Support
•    Produce the University of the Free State’s annual report to Department of Higher Education and Training (DHET), mid-term review report, and student enrolment plan, which are aligned with the academic risk register.
•    Steer the UFS to a forward-looking strategic institution by leading business intelligence information needs, translating complex institutional data into high-level briefings, providing predictive analytics, trend mapping, and data modelling
•    Facilitate HEMIS data submissions.
Global Benchmarking
•    Utilise institutional data for global positioning, supporting the university’s internationalisation mandate and rankings.
•    Manage data to be submitted to global rankings bodies.
Institutional Effectiveness and Optimisation
•    Lead institutional initiatives that identify operational bottlenecks and resource allocation efficiencies to drive overall institutional effectiveness.
•    Lead the Institutional Project Management Office.
•    Develop and maintain institutional project governance frameworks.
•    Coordinate, monitor and evaluate strategic institutional projects funded through the University's strategic initiatives.
•    Monitor institutional project performance, risks and benefits realisation.
•    Provide executive reports on strategic project implementation.
Institutional Strategy and Planning
•    Lead the development, implementation and monitoring of the University's Strategic Plan, Annual Performance Plan and institutional performance framework.
•    Coordinate institutional planning processes and monitor progress against strategic objectives.
•    Provide strategic advice to Executive Management on institutional performance, organisational effectiveness and strategic initiatives.
•    Lead institutional change management initiatives supporting strategic transformation.
Institutional Research and Business Intelligence
•    Direct institutional research and policy analysis to support executive decision-making.
•    Develop and maintain an integrated institutional management information and business intelligence environment.
•    Produce executive dashboards, strategic reports and institutional analyses that inform planning, policy development and performance improvement.
•    Promote evidence-based decision-making throughout the University.
Institutional Data Governance and Statutory Reporting
•    Provide strategic leadership for institutional data governance and data quality management.
•    Oversee HEMIS submissions and all statutory reporting to the Department of Higher Education and Training and other regulatory authorities.
•    Ensure compliance with legislative, audit and quality assurance requirements.
•    Develop institutional data policies, standards and governance frameworks.
Enrolment Planning and Performance Monitoring
•    Lead institutional enrolment planning and student performance analysis.
•    Develop forecasting models and strategic enrolment scenarios.
•    Monitor institutional performance indicators and benchmarking against national and international best practice.
•    Produce the University's Annual Report, Mid-term Review Report and other strategic institutional reports.
Stakeholder Engagement
•    Develop strategic partnerships with government departments, regulatory authorities, professional bodies, universities and national higher education structures.
•    Represent the University on institutional and national committees relating to planning, institutional research and higher education policy.
•    Manage data to be submitted to global rankings bodies
Leadership and Directorate Management
•    Provide strategic leadership to the Directorate.
•    Translate institutional strategy into operational plans and measurable performance outcomes.
•    Lead organisational development, succession planning, talent management and staff development.
•    Manage the Directorate's human, financial and physical resources in accordance with University policies.
Inherent Job Requirements
•    A relevant Doctoral qualification on NQF Level 10 in Higher Education Management, Strategy, Public Administration, Business Administration, Computer Science, Data Science, Information Systems or a related field.
•    A minimum of seven (7) years' experience within the higher education sector.
•    At least five (5) years in a senior strategic leadership role.
•    Experience in institutional strategy development and implementation.
•    Experience in institutional research and higher education policy analysis.
•    Experience in business intelligence and management information systems.
•    Experience in data governance, HEMIS and statutory reporting.
•    Experience in institutional project portfolio management.
•    Executive stakeholder engagement and organisational leadership experience.
Recommendations
•    A postgraduate qualification in Higher Education Management, Strategy, Public Administration, Business Administration, Computer Science, Data Science, Information Systems or a related field.
•    Knowledge of South African higher education policy, funding and quality assurance frameworks.
•    Experience in digital transformation, data analytics and institutional performance management.
•    Experience leading complex organisational change initiatives.
•    Advanced knowledge of business intelligence platforms and data visualisation.

Term of Appointment
The Senior Director will be appointed on a five-year fixed-term performance-based contract in accordance with the University's policies and procedures and may be eligible for reappointment subject to institutional requirements and performance.

Role Purpose
The Senior Collections Specialist is a hands-on, high-impact role responsible for driving collections performance improvement across client portfolios. The role sits at the intersection of strategy, analytics, and operations – taking ownership of net recovery optimisation, DebiCheck mandate management, payment gateway relationships, and the implementation of digital and process innovations that continuously evolve collections capability.
The successful candidate will be both a technical expert and a credible stakeholder partner – comfortable analysing collections data at a granular level and presenting findings and recommendations to senior leadership. This is a role for someone who wants to own outcomes, not just report on them.
Key Responsibilities
Collections Optimisation & Net Recovery
• Identify and implement strategies to improve net collection rates across client portfolios, balancing volume, timing, and cost of collection.
• Conduct root-cause analysis on collection failures, debit order returns, and underperforming segments to develop targeted interventions.
• Design and monitor collection strategies by customer segment – including payment date optimisation, retry logic, and contact sequencing.
• Track and report on collection KPIs (first-attempt success rate, overall collection rate, cost-per-rand collected) and drive continuous improvement against benchmarks.
• Evaluate the net benefit impact of strategic changes before implementation and measure outcomes post-deployment.
Process Improvement & Innovation
• Identify inefficiencies in existing collections workflows and lead the design and implementation of process improvements.
• Build and maintain a structured innovation pipeline – evaluating emerging tools, approaches, and technologies for applicability to the collections environment.
• Define and drive a digital collections roadmap, incorporating channel diversification (WhatsApp, USSD, self-serve portals), automated retry logic, and AI-assisted prioritisation.
• Partner with technology and product teams to translate strategy into system requirements, user stories, and operational change.
• Lead business change management for collections initiatives – engaging internal and client stakeholders on process changes, system enhancements, and performance outcomes.
DebiCheck & Payment Method Optimisation
• Own the DebiCheck mandate strategy – driving improvements in mandate uptake rates, authentication success, and mandate retention across the lifecycle.
• Analyse and address DebiCheck decline reasons (Suspension, Dispute, Technical, Expiry, etc.) to build targeted remediation approaches by decline category.
• Monitor DebiCheck mandate health across the portfolio – tracking dormant, expired, and failed mandates and designing re-instatement campaigns.
• Stay current with PASA regulatory requirements and industry developments affecting DebiCheck and debit order processing, ensuring full compliance.
• Evaluate and recommend additional payment method strategies (EFT, real-time payments, digital wallets) to complement existing debit order capabilities and improve collection reach.
Payment Gateway & Provider Management
• Manage relationships with external payment service providers, including negotiating SLAs, reviewing service catalogues, and overseeing performance against contractual commitments.
• Monitor payment gateway performance metrics – success rates, processing times, error rates — and escalate issues or drive remediation where performance falls below threshold.
• Evaluate new or alternative payment gateway providers and make recommendations based on capability, cost, and strategic fit.
• Serve as the internal subject matter expert on payment processing flows, reconciliation, and exception handling, supporting client queries and internal escalations.
Reporting & Data Analytics
• Reporting & Data Analytics
• Design and maintain MIS and BI reporting for collections performance — covering operational dashboards, executive summaries, and ad hoc deep-dives.
• Build and validate data extracts and analytical models using SQL, SAS, and Advanced Excel to support strategy design and performance monitoring.
• Present collections performance and strategic recommendations at client and internal management forums, translating complex data into clear business insights.
• Maintain data quality and consistency across reporting outputs, working with data engineering teams where necessary.
Stakeholder Management

• Collaborate cross-functionally with sales, product, customer service, and marketing teams to align collections initiatives with broader business objectives.
• Manage and influence without direct authority – influencing internal and client workstreams to deliver collections outcomes in a matrix environment.

• Minimum 5–7 years' experience in a collections strategy, premium collections, or payment operations role within financial services (insurance, banking, or fintech).

• Hands-on experience with DebiCheck – including mandate management, authentication flows, decline categorisation, and PASA compliance requirements.
• Experience managing or working closely with external payment service providers or collection system vendors.

Technical Skills

Role Overview The Logistics Coordinator is a pivotal role within the business, responsible for the end-to-end coordination of magnetite product movements from mine gate in South Africa through to final delivery at international destinations. Operating at the intersection of operations, finance, and commercial, the successful candidate will ensure that product flows efficiently, documentation is accurate, and all stakeholders — from mine producers to international shipping partners are kept informed and aligned throughout the logistics chain.
This role demands a proactive, detail-oriented professional who thrives in a multi stakeholder environment and is comfortable managing competing priorities across time zones, currencies, and regulatory frameworks.
Responsibilities:
Mine & Producer Liaison:
Maintain regular communication with mine producers and export agents to confirm scheduled loadings, dispatch dates and product availability.
Coordinate product grade and quality requirements against customer specifications and offtake agreement parameters.
Manage daily and weekly production and dispatch schedules, escalating deviations to the Operations Manager promptly.
Maintain an up-to-date mine-to-port tracker covering all active shipments
Transport & Domestic Logistics:
Engage and manage approved domestic transport contractors (road haulage and rail) for the movement of magnetite product.
Issue transport instructions, confirm bookings and monitor vehicle/wagon movements in real time.
Investigate and resolve transport delays, shortfalls, and quality discrepancies in transit.
Track and reconcile truck and rail tonnages against dispatch and receipt records.
Export Documentation & Compliance:
Prepare, review and submit all required export documentation in accordance with South African customs (SARS) and international trade regulations.
Coordinate with freight forwarders and clearing agents to ensure timeous clearance at loading ports.
Maintain a document tracking register ensuring all originals and copies are filed and accessible for audit purposes.
Stay current with SARS, ITAC and port authority regulatory changes affecting magnetite export.
International Shipping Management:
Coordinate cargo bookings with international shipping lines and freight forwarders; confirm vessel nominations and sailing schedules.
Liaise with port agents at loading and discharge ports to manage vessel operations and demurrage exposure.
Monitor vessel ETDs, ETAs and notify all relevant parties of changes affecting downstream logistics.
Review and negotiate freight rates in conjunction with the commercial team; maintain a freight rate and surcharge register.
Track and resolve any claims arising from cargo damage, short-landing or contamination.
Laboratory & Quality Coordination:
Engage accredited laboratory services for independent survey and sampling of magnetite product at load and discharge ports.
Obtain and distribute Certificates of Analysis, surveyor reports and weight certificates to customers, finance teams and internal stakeholders.
Proactively flag quality deviations against offtake agreement specifications and support any claims resolution process.
Maintain a quality results database linked to shipment records.
Finance & Treasury Interface:
Provide logistics cost data (freight, transport, port charges, laboratory fees) to the finance team for accurate accrual and invoice processing.
Review and approve third-party freight and logistics invoices against agreed rates and confirmed quantities.
Support the treasury function with shipping documentation required for foreign currency payments and letters of credit.
Coordinate intercompany logistics cost allocations between South African, Mauritius, and other group entities.
Assist in reconciling logistics costs against standard costs and flagging variances to the cost accounting team.
Reporting & Systems Administration;
Maintain Sage ERP with accurate and timely capture of despatch, receipt and cost transactions related to logistics.
Produce weekly and monthly logistics reports including shipment status, cost summaries and KPI dashboards for management.
Update internal trackers for vessel nominations, document status, payment milestones and claims.
Support internal and external audit processes by maintaining a complete and organised document archive.
Contribute to continuous improvement of logistics processes, systems and reporting tools.

about_role:
ROLE PURPOSE
The Senior Infrastructure Demand Management – Server Lead is accountable for end‑to‑end ownership and governance of server infrastructure demand across physical, virtual, and cloud environments. The role provides senior technical and service leadership to ensure that infrastructure demand is optimally planned, prioritised, governed, and delivered in alignment with business strategy, client commitments, security standards, and service management frameworks.
The incumbent acts as the primary authority on server demand intake, demand shaping, and delivery readiness, translating complex business and project requirements into executable infrastructure demand plans. The role operates with a high degree of autonomy, influencing delivery outcomes across multiple technical teams, and ensuring infrastructure demand is delivered predictably, compliantly, and at scale.
ROLE REQUIREMENT
• Strategic Infrastructure Demand Ownership
• Own and govern the server infrastructure demand pipeline across physical, virtual, and cloud platforms.
• Shape demand through early engagement with business, programme, and project stakeholders to ensure feasibility, cost awareness, and technical alignment.
• Act as the senior escalation point for complex or high‑risk infrastructure demand initiatives.
• Influence prioritisation decisions to balance capacity, risk, cost, and delivery commitments.
• Senior Build Governance & Delivery Enablement
• Translate approved demand into standardised, scalable build architectures and demand artefacts for execution by infrastructure engineering teams.
• Provide senior oversight of server build readiness, ensuring all technical, security, and operational prerequisites are met before execution.
• Govern complex builds, migrations, and environment expansions, including hybrid and cloud‑integrated solutions.
• Ensure infrastructure delivery adheres to agreed architectural, operational, and service standards.
• Service Management Leadership & SLA Assurance
• Provide senior operational leadership across the full lifecycle of infrastructure requests, from demand intake to production handover.
• Monitor delivery performance against SLAs, KPIs, and contractual commitments, proactively addressing systemic issues.
• Drive alignment with ITIL practices across Incident, Change, Problem, and Release processes.
• Champion service stability, predictability, and continuous service improvement.
• CMDB, Data Integrity & Asset Governance
• Own the accuracy, integrity, and auditability of server configuration items within the CMDB.
• Define and enforce standards for CI lifecycle management, data quality, and reconciliation.
• Lead investigations into CMDB discrepancies and implement corrective and preventative actions.
• Ensure infrastructure assets are fully traceable, compliant, and governance‑ready at all times.
• Security, Compliance & Risk Management
• Ensure all server infrastructure demand complies with organisational security, risk, and regulatory requirements prior to production release.
• Coordinate senior‑level sign‑offs with Information Security, Risk, and Compliance stakeholders.
• Identify infrastructure‑related risks early and drive mitigation strategies across delivery teams.
• Support internal and external audits by providing authoritative infrastructure evidence and documentation.
• Reporting, Optimization & Continuous Improvement
• Produce executive‑level reporting on infrastructure demand trends, delivery performance, capacity constraints, and risk exposure.
• Analyze demand data to inform forecasting, capacity planning, and investment decisions.
• Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on automation, standardization, and process efficiency.
• Act as a thought leader within infrastructure demand management, contributing to best practice and maturity uplift.
PROFESSIONAL COMPETENCIES
• Deep understanding of Windows and Linux server environments (physical, virtual, and cloud)

• Strong exposure to cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure, or equivalent)
• Expert use of ITSM tools (e.g. BMC Remedy, ServiceNow, Jira)
• Strong command of ITIL‑aligned service management practices
• Advanced understanding of CMDB architecture and configuration management
• Ability to translate technical complexity into business‑relevant insights
QUALIFICATIONS & EXPERIENCE
• Grade 12
• Diploma or Degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, or related discipline
• 10–15 years’ experience in enterprise ICT infrastructure, with demonstrated senior accountability
• 5+ years’ experience operating in complex, multi‑stakeholder delivery or project environments
• ITIL Foundation certification (required); ITIL Intermediate or equivalent advantageous
• Proven experience across server hardware, operating systems, storage, and networking
• Enterprise‑scale exposure to hybrid and cloud infrastructure environments Experience in server infrastructure (hardware, OS, storage, networking)

job_title: High-Ticket Sales Closer — Inbound, Remote (Australian Company)
about_role:
LicencePath is hiring experienced high-ticket closers for inbound calls only.
• $2,100 AUD per enrolment commissions. Uncapped.

About LicencePath
We help experienced tradies and workers — carpenters, electricians, bricklayers and more — get their trade certificate and licence so they can take the next step in their career.
This is a regulated industry and a legal requirement for every tradie to have. Plenty of good tradesmen have the skills and the years on the tools but not the piece of paper the government requires to work for themselves, charge properly, or run their own jobs. We close that gap — through short-course gap-training and recognition of the experience they already have — and get them licensed much faster than the traditional way. We're talking years to weeks.
For the tradesman, a licence changes everything: their own contracts, uncapped income, the freedom to run their own show. For you, it's a sales role you can actually stand behind. You're not talking anyone into anything they don't need — you're helping someone unlock the career they've already earned. That's rare in sales, and it makes the job easier and the money better.
We have our own blue ocean, focusing on specific licences that are very difficult for anyone else to offer. There's barely any competition. So it's not hard to show people the value in this.
The role
We're hiring experienced high-ticket closers for inbound calls only.
Every lead has already filled out an eligibility form to check whether they can get their trade licence through gap-training or experience. So they've put their hand up before you ever speak to them. No cold calling. No prospecting. No chasing dead leads.
Your job: get on the phone, explain the process, handle the objections, and move them down the line toward getting licensed.
These are government-regulated licences — a legal requirement to work in their trade. The customer needs this. We just make it faster and simpler than doing it alone. That makes the sale close to a no-brainer, and your job is to push it over the line.
What you'll do
• Take inbound calls from people who've already checked their eligibility
• Explain the pathway clearly, in plain language
• Handle the objections that come up — price, time, requirements
• Guide them through commitment and enrolment
• Keep momentum: every lead called fast, every deal followed through
Who we want
• You've closed high-ticket over the phone before — real deals, real objections, real money.
• You hold a price. You don't fold the moment someone pushes for a discount.
• You can talk to a tradesman. Our customers are blunt and sceptical.
• Clear, confident English on the phone.
• You know how to work a sales cycle.
• You understand the importance of speed to lead.
• You're a hunter — not someone looking for a clock-on, clock-off job. You understand that when a lead comes in, that's a $2,100 phone call waiting, and you're not going to let it sit until it burns.
WHY THE PRODUCT SELLS
These are government-regulated licences. A legal requirement, not a nice-to-have. We focus on specific licences that are difficult for anyone else to offer, so there is very little competition. You are not talking anyone into something they do not need.

• Verification of codes etc. for incoming stock
